documents.title: Finland National Basic Income Experiment (Kela 2017–2018)
documents.summary: Finland provided €560 monthly unconditional tax-free basic income to 2,000 unemployed individuals for two years to study employment participation and subjective well-being.
documents.evidence: Recipients experienced significantly higher levels of life satisfaction, mental resilience, lower cortisol/stress levels, and greater financial confidence compared to the control group. Employment gains were statistically modest (recipients worked an average of 6 additional days per year).
citations: Kela (Social Insurance Institution of Finland), Final Report on the Finnish Basic Income Experiment, 2020

documents.title: Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend (PFD): Macroeconomic Effects
documents.summary: Operating since 1982, distributing universal annual cash dividends ($1,000 to $3,200 per resident) funded from state mineral royalties to all Alaskan residents regardless of employment.
documents.evidence: NBER analysis demonstrated that universal unconditional cash transfers did not diminish full-time aggregate employment; instead, part-time work expanded by 17%, and increased local purchasing power created consumer service jobs that balanced voluntary reductions in marginal hours.
citations: National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), 'The Effect of a Universal Cash Transfer on Employment: Evidence from the Alaska Permanent Fund', 2018

documents.title: Fiscal Feasibility & Tax Burden of Nationwide UBI
documents.summary: Calculations on the budgetary cost of universal basic income for adult populations and the trade-offs with existing targeted programs.
documents.evidence: A standard $1,000/month UBI for 258 million adult Americans requires approximately $3.1 trillion annually—equivalent to roughly 75% of total federal tax revenues. Paying for it without slashing core healthcare and disability transfers would require doubling federal income taxes or enacting an aggressive 15–20% Value Added Tax (VAT).
citations: Congressional Budget Office (CBO), Working Paper on Universal Cash Transfers, 2023
Tax Foundation, 'Modeling Universal Basic Income Options', 2022

documents.title: The Welfare Trap & Administrative Overhead of Means-Testing
documents.summary: Means-tested welfare programs impose high marginal effective tax rates (METRs) on the working poor, creating perverse disincentives to seek employment.
documents.evidence: Beneficiaries under TANF, SNAP, and housing vouchers frequently face effective marginal tax rates between 70% and 95% due to abrupt benefit phase-outs when wage income rises. Administrative overhead in means-testing consumes 8% to 14% of overall welfare program budgets, whereas direct cash transfers consume under 2%.
citations: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities (CBPP), 'Marginal Tax Rates on Low-Income Families', 2023
